title: Billing and Late Charge Terms Across Workplace Cafe Management Program Service Models
content:
Fixed terms. For each service model of the Workplace Cafe Management Program, this schedule fixes the invoicing cycle, the calendar days from the invoice date within which payment is due, the monthly late charge taken on an overdue invoice as a percentage of the overdue amount, the calendar days past the due date before a late charge may be raised, the ceiling on the late charge raised against one invoice, and the days past due at which the contract is escalated for credit hold.

1. Figures by service model

| Service model | Invoicing cycle | Payment terms (calendar days) | Monthly late charge (per cent of overdue amount) | Late charge grace (calendar days) | Late charge ceiling per invoice (USD) | Credit hold threshold (days past due) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grab & Go Cafe Service | monthly | 15 | 1.5 | 3 | 500.00 | 45 |
| Limited Service Cafe | monthly | 21 | 1.5 | 5 | 950.00 | 60 |
| Full Service Cafe | monthly | 30 | 1.25 | 7 | 2400.00 | 75 |
| Culinary Center Cafe | monthly | 30 | 1.0 | 10 | 4800.00 | 90 |
| Executive Dining Service | semimonthly | 45 | 1.0 | 10 | 5600.00 | 90 |
| Campus Dining Commons Service | semimonthly | 45 | 0.85 | 14 | 9500.00 | 120 |

2. Notes distinguishing the models

The invoicing cycle changes only once across the family, from monthly at the four lighter-touch models to semimonthly at Executive Dining Service and Campus Dining Commons Service. Payment terms, late charge grace and the credit hold threshold all lengthen moving toward the larger models, while the monthly late charge percentage moves the other way, falling from 1.5 per cent at the two smallest models to 0.85 per cent at Campus Dining Commons Service. Full Service Cafe and Culinary Center Cafe share the same payment terms of 30 calendar days but differ in every other figure this table records, and Culinary Center Cafe shares its monthly late charge percentage and late charge grace period with Executive Dining Service despite the two models sitting on different invoicing cycles.

3. Reading the schedule, hypothetically

Suppose an invoice issued to a site under Culinary Center Cafe fell 12 calendar days past its due date. Hypothetically, that would be beyond the 10 calendar days of grace this table fixes for that service model, so a late charge could be raised at the monthly rate of 1.0 per cent of the overdue amount, subject to the ceiling of 4800.00 USD this table fixes against one invoice, and the account would still sit well short of the 90 days past due at which this table's credit hold threshold for that service model is reached.
